title: Making endpoint activity visible.
intro: A self-hosted monitoring lab that connects file changes and failed SSH logins to actionable security alerts.
context: Security monitoring starts with understanding what an endpoint is doing. This lab explores that workflow in a controlled Ubuntu virtual machine.
approach: Configured the Wazuh manager, indexer, and dashboard in an Ubuntu virtual environment.
Set up real-time file-integrity monitoring and tested file changes.
Simulated failed SSH logins, reviewed detection rules and MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and configured Postfix email alerts.
outcome: The project documents an end-to-end monitoring and alerting workflow, from a controlled endpoint event to investigation in Wazuh.
limits: Self-hosted training environment; this is not a claim of operating a production SOC.

title: Files encrypted before they leave.
intro: A file-sharing prototype exploring browser-side encryption, direct object storage transfers, and share-link key handling.
context: Sharing a file should involve thinking about where its contents and keys travel. This prototype explores that boundary with encryption in the browser.
approach: Implemented browser-side AES-256-GCM encryption for files and filenames.
Used S3 presigned URLs for direct uploads and downloads.
Passed decryption keys in URL fragments and implemented expiry and download-limit checks.
outcome: A documented prototype joining client-side cryptography with a cloud storage workflow.
limits: Educational prototype; no independent cryptographic audit or production-readiness claim. Sharing a complete link also shares access to its key.

title: A connection when networks disappear.
intro: An offline Android proof of concept for nearby SOS messages and GPS sharing during connectivity loss.
context: Disasters can interrupt mobile and internet service. This project investigates local device-to-device communication when conventional connectivity is unavailable.
approach: Built an Android interface with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
Used Nearby Connections for local peer discovery and SOS/location messages.
Tested offline communication across two physical Android devices.
outcome: A working proof of concept for local discovery and emergency-message exchange without internet access.
limits: Research prototype, not an emergency service. Range, device compatibility, delivery, and availability are not guaranteed. Roadmap features are not presented as delivered.

title: Exploring AI that can explain itself.
intro: A team research prototype combining medical-image classification, segmentation, and visual explanations.
context: My final-year project explored deep learning for intracranial aneurysm detection and the challenge of explaining a model's predictions.
approach: Co-developed a ResNet-50 classification and U-Net segmentation pipeline.
Used Grad-CAM to visualize regions associated with model predictions.
Connected model inference to a Flask API and a React review interface.
outcome: An academic research prototype spanning model development, explainability, and a web-based review workflow.
limits: Academic research only, not a clinically validated diagnostic tool. Performance figures are omitted because the original evaluation report is not available in the supporting portfolio materials.

title: From a finding to a clear remediation.
intro: A scoped security assessment of a deliberately vulnerable local application, with findings and remediation priorities.
context: The exercise focuses on reproducing vulnerabilities and explaining their impact within a safe, intentionally vulnerable training environment.
approach: Ran OWASP Juice Shop locally with Docker and assessed it using OWASP ZAP.
Reproduced SQL injection authentication bypass and DOM-based XSS.
Reviewed token storage, headers, and CSRF behavior, separating confirmed findings from inconclusive tests.
outcome: A documented assessment that distinguishes reproducible vulnerabilities from hardening observations and unconfirmed behavior.
limits: Local OWASP Juice Shop only. No third-party production or staging systems are claimed as part of the authorized assessment.

title: Thinking through the sign-in boundary.
intro: A Node.js authentication prototype combining Google sign-in, time-based second factors, and sensitive-field encryption.
context: Authentication brings identity, sessions, and secrets together. This project explores those concerns through a small application prototype.
approach: Integrated Google OAuth 2.0 using Passport.js.
Added TOTP two-factor verification.
Used AES-256-GCM to encrypt sensitive fields in a SQLite-backed application.
outcome: A practical identity-flow prototype with documented implementation decisions.
limits: A learning project, not a certified identity provider or independently audited authentication service.

title: Understanding cloud controls in context.
intro: An Azure security demonstration covering access boundaries, storage configuration, and web-application firewall setup.
context: Cloud security controls need to be understood as part of a configuration, with clear scope and limitations.
approach: Reviewed IAM, storage settings, and Defender for Cloud recommendations.
Applied resource-scoped access and configured geo-redundant storage.
Provisioned Application Gateway WAF_v2 with managed rules in detection mode.
outcome: A non-production configuration exercise documenting cloud security controls and deployment constraints.
limits: Detection mode with a placeholder backend. This project does not claim to have protected live production traffic.

title: A clearer path from detection to recovery.
intro: A documented response plan with responsibilities, escalation paths, and a ransomware tabletop scenario.
context: An incident response plan should help people understand what to do and who is responsible before an incident occurs.
approach: Defined response stages, incident severity tiers, and a CSIRT responsibility matrix.
Mapped a ransomware tabletop scenario to MITRE ATT&CK.
Prepared security-awareness and staff-training materials.
outcome: A structured set of procedures for a simulated incident lifecycle, from detection and containment to recovery.
limits: Training and planning materials; no claim of responding to a real organizational ransomware incident.

title: Learning from a controlled awareness test.
intro: A consent-based exercise using two self-owned email accounts to study delivery and spam-filter behavior.
context: A small controlled test can reveal how an awareness exercise behaves without exposing unsuspecting people.
approach: Configured a controlled GoPhish exercise using self-owned test accounts.
Observed message delivery and Gmail spam interception.
Documented the small sample and the limits of the results.
outcome: A documented exercise in safe simulation design and communicating what the evidence can support.
limits: Two self-owned addresses; results do not establish organization-wide click rates or awareness effectiveness.

title: An introduction to visual classification.
intro: A team-built CNN project for facial-expression classification with image preprocessing and command-line inference.
context: This project provided practical experience with image handling, convolutional models, and inference workflows.
approach: Contributed to a CNN-based classification workflow in Python.
Used TensorFlow/Keras for model development and OpenCV for image handling.
Worked on a command-line inference workflow.
outcome: A learning project connecting computer-vision preprocessing with model inference.
limits: An educational classifier, not a reliable measure of a person's internal emotional state or a tool for consequential decisions.

title: A familiar interface, built component by component.
intro: A Spotify-inspired frontend exploring reusable components, shared player state, and routing.
context: The project uses a familiar music interface to practice frontend structure and interactive state management.
approach: Built reusable album, song-list, and player components.
Managed shared playback state with React Context API.
Added route-based navigation and a modular project structure.
outcome: A frontend learning project with a coherent browsing and playback interface.
limits: Independent educational project, not affiliated with Spotify. Third-party names and content remain with their respective owners.

title: An early step in building for the web.
intro: An earlier portfolio repository documenting the start of my web-development journey.
context: Kept as part of the project archive to show the progression from an early personal site to more focused technical work.
approach: Created an early personal portfolio website.
Maintained the project in a public GitHub repository.
outcome: An archived example of earlier web work.
limits: Historical project; current professional information is on this portfolio.

title: Practicing programming through a quiz.
intro: An early Java quiz repository from my programming-learning journey.
context: An introductory project preserved alongside later security, software, and AI work.
approach: Built an introductory quiz project in Java.
Published the source in a dedicated GitHub repository.
limits: Descriptions are limited to the supplied repository listing; additional implementation details have not been verified.
